package: Bug Evolution Lab — Act I visual polish
notes: Scene 04 is the static four-frame sequence exported by buglab.crossover_slides.

scenes.name: 01_beetle_model
scenes.title: A genome becomes movement
scenes.educational_message: A genome is a sequence of turn commands that produces a trajectory.

scenes.name: 02_population
scenes.title: Different genomes explore different paths
scenes.educational_message: Different genomes produce different trajectories under identical physics.

scenes.name: 03_evaluation_selection
scenes.title: Evaluate, then select parents
scenes.educational_message: The introductory score uses the closest straight-line approach over the complete trajectory.

scenes.name: 05_one_generation_transition
scenes.title: One generation update, step by step
scenes.educational_message: One update evaluates a population, selects parents, creates offspring, and evaluates the complete next generation.

scenes.name: 06_simple_evolution
scenes.title: Repeated generations can improve the search
scenes.educational_message: Recorded populations move, pause at evaluation, and then transition to the next generation.

scenes.name: 07_two_bridges_evolution
scenes.title: A population can explore two barrier openings
scenes.educational_message: Colors identify physically crossed openings, independently of whether the goal was reached.

scenes.name: 08_method_comparison
scenes.title: Three search strategies, one shared problem
scenes.educational_message: GA evolves populations, random search draws independent batches, and local search tests neighbors of an incumbent.

scenes.name: 09_spiral_fitness_problem
scenes.title: When closest approach is not useful progress
scenes.educational_message: Minimum-over-trajectory straight-line distance can favor a wall-separated approach and penalize a necessary detour.
